building-immunology.headline: Connecting buildings and human health.
building-immunology.title: One room. A responsive building.
building-immunology.imageAlt: Archived room-level risk interface from the supplied presentation, showing a selected room and its labeled risk category.
building-immunology.sceneAlt: Future concept: an occupied building connects microbial observations, room sensing, a digital model, and thermal conditions.
building-immunology.description: Microbial observations and room-level modeling address separate local questions. Linking measurements, actionable models and occupant needs calls for microbiology, building science, simulation, facility operations and human-factors expertise. A cutaway occupied building connects microbes, sensing, a digital model and thermal conditions. The illustration describes a shared research vision, not an installed autonomous building controller or a validated calibration between the separate studies.

disinfection-robot.headline: Disinfection starts with the surface.
disinfection-robot.title: One surface. Building-wide care.
disinfection-robot.imageAlt: Still from the supplied Wiley research infographic, linking surface-material recognition to transmission modeling and adapted treatment.
disinfection-robot.sceneAlt: Future concept: a mobile manipulator treats a table while navigating around furniture and an occupant.
disinfection-robot.description: The published framework connects material recognition with transmission modeling and treatment decisions. Delivering compatible treatment, navigating occupied rooms and verifying outcomes require materials, infection-control, navigation, human-factors and facility expertise. The concept scene shows a mobile manipulator approaching a table while a person occupies the room. The supplied animations and mapping examples do not establish a complete deployed system or measured pathogen removal.

surgery-ai.headline: Advancing Physical AI for Clearer Vision in Minimally Invasive Surgery
surgery-ai.title: One camera. Continuous visual assistance.
surgery-ai.imageAlt: Laboratory robot-mounted actuator above an abdominal model, from the original prototype recording.
surgery-ai.future: Camera motion, lens care & the surgeon
surgery-ai.sceneAlt: Future concept: external actuation, an internal camera, lens care, and visual feedback connect to the surgeon.
surgery-ai.description: The current benchtop prototype explores external actuation of an internal camera. Lens care, visual interpretation and integration into the procedure require soft robotics, materials, computer vision, control, surgeons and clinical evaluation. A concept diagram connects an actuator and internal camera with a cleaning flow, display and surgeon. The positioning demonstration and proposed cleaning architecture are separate; clinical outcomes are not established.

robotic-block-assembly.headline: Coastal resilience, block by block.
robotic-block-assembly.title: One joint. A resilient coastline.
robotic-block-assembly.imageAlt: Source presentation showing several module joints and their pick, place and interlock sequences.
robotic-block-assembly.sceneAlt: Frame from the opening Isaac Sim video: a tracked excavator beside seven interlocking TPMS modules forming a breakwater segment on a sandy shoreline. Kinematic concept visualization.
robotic-block-assembly.description: The supplied work presents interlocking module and robotic assembly concepts. Durable materials, reliable assembly and coastal evaluation must connect materials science, coastal engineering, robotics, construction and field teams. The shared-vision image is a frame from the opening Isaac Sim video after six prescribed placements beside a starter module. The excavator holds its clamp clear of the completed row on the rendered shoreline. This kinematic concept illustrates the larger vision; it does not establish physical assembly, wave performance or field durability.

disease-resistant-school-communities.headline: Disease-Resistant School Communities
disease-resistant-school-communities.title: From one classroom to a healthier community.
disease-resistant-school-communities.imageAlt: School students use gloves and sampling materials to collect samples from indoor surfaces.
disease-resistant-school-communities.sceneAlt: An animated classroom from the supplied research film, illustrating the shared goal of healthier learning environments.
disease-resistant-school-communities.description: The current evidence consists of student environmental-sampling activities and separate studies modeling school infection risk and ventilation energy costs. Moving toward healthier school communities requires student and educator participation, microbiology, building science and school operations, and family and community input. The shared-vision classroom is an illustration from the supplied film. It does not document an adopted intervention or measured improvement in health, learning or energy use.

healthy-built-environments.headline: AI-Empowered Healthy Built Environments
healthy-built-environments.title: From room models to responsive buildings.
healthy-built-environments.current: Model the room and its use
healthy-built-environments.imageAlt: Overhead view of an indoor building model, with furniture, rooms, and service layers.
healthy-built-environments.sceneAlt: Future concept: an occupied building connects environmental sensing, a digital model, and thermal conditions around people.
healthy-built-environments.description: Published room-level models and separate recorded demonstrations are the starting point. Building scientists, sensing specialists and AI researchers must connect observations with predictions. Controls, robotics and facility operators must establish feasible interventions. Occupants, human-factors researchers and interaction designers must shape useful responses. The future concept is a building that anticipates environmental challenges while respecting human health, comfort and everyday needs; it is not an installed autonomous system.
